doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Brother-in-law's string band, mandolin and Joe Venuti
summary: Williams learns guitar and mandolin from his brother-in-law, plays bass, then switches to violin after hearing Joe Venuti in Muskogee.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Tell me, you’ve been playing for a long time, a lot of great music, with a lot of great performers. What first attracted you to the guitar and the violin?

Well my brother-in-law was, knew quite a bit about strings and he started me out on, you know, we used to sit around the house and play old blues on guitar, and I’d watch him. And when he’d put the guitar down I’d pick it up and play blues. And he saw that I was interested, and he went and bought a mandolin and he would pick the melody on the mandolin and show me the changes on the guitar. So I actually played guitar. I got where I was pretty good but when he’d lay the mandolin down, I’d pick it up and play that. And going from the mandolin to, and he needed a bass in his string band, not knowing that a cello was too light, you know, it was also a lead instrument. But we got the cello and took the strings off and put bass strings on the cello. And I played bass, until Joe Venuti came through Muskogee. I heard him. He played at an outdoors pavilion. I was about half a block from him, you know, close as I could get you know? And I told my mother, “That’s what I want to play.” So the next day they changed the cello and brought me a violin home. And no problem, I played the violin. Because it’s the same as the mandolin, you know, E-A-D-G you know? The mandolin got double strings, and you pick that. So I just picked up the fiddle and started playing. And they often asked me to, some of them, to play the first tune I remember playing on the violin. And the name of that tune was “You Got To See Your Mama Every Night Or You Can’t See Your Mama At All.”
